text: For a proposed crypto-bot monitor drill suite, run a synthetic baseline and then repeat the workload with faults such as dependency disconnection, latency, process restart or thread stalls. This adapts fault-injection practices demonstrated by Microsoft and WarpStream; it is a design recommendation, not evidence of an existing bot implementation. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: More aggressive fault injection is not automatically better coverage. FoundationDB tunes fault distributions because excessive fault rates can confine execution to a small state space; monitor drills should therefore include intervals in which useful work and recovery can proceed. The monitor recommendation is an inference. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Deterministic failure replay requires control over nondeterministic inputs, including time, random choices, scheduling and I/O. For a bot monitor, the inferred design is to control these inputs at its dependency boundaries; replaying price records alone does not establish deterministic execution. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: A drill needs a correctness oracle, not merely an absence of crashes. FoundationDB uses workload and local assertions; WarpStream checks message identity and monotonic sequences. Applied to a bot monitor, define expected outcomes and invariant violations before injecting each failure. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: A deterministic simulator still needs controlled substitutes for external dependencies. It cannot by itself establish that the real external integration behaves like its mocks; this limits what a simulated exchange can establish about a live crypto venue. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Deterministic replay does not guarantee that the same scenario reaches the same failure after changing the binary. In its March 2024 investigation, Cockroach Labs reported instrumentation and code changes could change the terminal state; the investigation ultimately produced a reproducing unit test. The inferred practice is to preserve the failing build and scenario and add a focused regression test for the fix. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Market-data replay is not proof of realistic execution: HftBacktest states that replay cannot change market data or model market impact, and that some partial-fill scenarios remain unrealistic. Use such replay to exercise monitor behavior under recorded inputs; do not treat its fills as proof of what live orders would do. The monitor-use recommendation is an inference. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Simulation correctness results do not establish production performance or fidelity to every dependency. The FoundationDB paper states its simulator cannot reliably detect performance problems and cannot test dependencies outside its simulation-compatible implementation. Antithesis also requires external dependencies to be controlled. For a monitor, supplement deterministic drills with checks against real dependency behavior. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: A rare failure can require correlated faults and internal transitions that ordinary stress testing misses. Cockroach Labs describes a bug diagnosed using deterministic replay and traces; WarpStream describes a failure plus scheduling race found by its fault-injecting simulator. This supports testing adversarial event orderings for monitor code, without implying a guaranteed bug-detection rate. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Freqtrade documents that backtesting simulates only part of its live execution logic and that callback frequency can differ between backtesting and live iterations. A monitor drill should exercise operational behavior directly instead of treating matching backtest output as sufficient verification. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Use a fault matrix that includes process restarts, network partitions, latency and delayed execution, and exercise combinations rather than only isolated failures. This is an inferred monitor-drill pattern: FoundationDB injects these classes of faults, and WarpStream describes a data-loss bug requiring both a failed flush and a rare thread interleaving. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Define the simulation boundary explicitly: external dependencies must be mocked or otherwise controlled for determinism. WarpStream included clients, control-plane nodes and local storage dependencies in its test topology. Applied to a bot monitor, include controlled dependency responses and failures in the harness rather than assuming a deterministic monitor process controls external services. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Game-day drills can validate monitoring systems and human incident processes together. Microsoft describes coordinated outage simulations with fault injection, and recommends testing first in pre-production, restricting blast radius and retaining a way to end an experiment. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: In a historical Freqtrade issue, the reporter described different dry-run and backtest results; a project member proposed resampling and the smaller live data window as the likely explanation, explicitly describing the explanation as an assumption. This is a candidate regression scenario, not a confirmed current defect. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Workload quality limits DST: many executions do not establish broad state-space exploration. Antithesis identifies exploration as a separate technical challenge, and Phil Eaton warns that workload design and the fidelity of mocked failures determine what the tests can expose. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: A recovery drill should restore dependencies to a recoverable condition and assert eventual recovery. FoundationDB explicitly tests this property after failures; this provides a model for a monitor drill that checks recovery after the injected outage ends. (low confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay

text: Vary seeds, workloads and configurations, then inspect coverage to find missing scenarios. FoundationDB varies configurations and injection parameters and measures conditional coverage; Antithesis documents repeated seeded simulation and invariant checking. For a monitor, preserve a failing scenario and broaden future runs beyond that single replay. (medium confidence)
keywords: Crypto bot monitor failure drills and deterministic replay
